avatar.$about: Avatar: who or what something belongs to. Shows a picture, falls back to initials, then to an icon. Every value is a token reference, a plain even number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025).
avatar.title: Avatar
avatar.anatomy: One face: a picture, or initials on a tinted fill, or an icon. Optional status dot on the edge. A group stacks faces with overlap and ends with a +N face. The face carries the border/primary edge; the status dot sits outside it so it is never clipped.

rules.fallback: Three layers, in order: the picture; initials from the name; an icon (Lucide user) when there is no name. The fallback is always painted underneath, so a slow or broken picture never leaves a hole. The picture fades in at duration/fast when it has loaded; if it fails, the fallback stays. Initials are the first letter of the first and last word: one letter at 2xs and xs, two from sm up.
rules.tone: The fill of a fallback is picked from the name, so the same name always gets the same colour. Five tones: neutral, brand, success, warning, info, each fill/*-secondary with content/*. Critical is left out (red reads as an error) and so is purple (D-015). A tone prop overrides the pick.
rules.sizes: Six sizes taken from the size tokens: 2xs 20 (icon/md), xs 24 (icon/lg), sm 32 (control/xs, the side nav profile), md 40 (control/sm, the default), lg 48 (control/md), xl 56 (control/lg). 20 and 24 sit in a line of text or a dense list and show one initial; 32 to 56 stand alone. Above 56 an avatar is a picture, not a component size. Initial type grows with the face: 10, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20.
rules.shape: Circle (radius/full) for people. Squircle for brands, products and workspaces: radius is size × 0.3, to the nearest 2 under 12 and the nearest 4 above (6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 16). The 0.3 matches the side nav brand logo (40, radius/lg 12). Set values, listed per size.
rules.edge: A 1px border/primary edge drawn over the picture, inside the face, so a picture that is the same colour as the surface still has an outline (as the side nav profile). It sits on the media layer, after the picture.
rules.status: Four statuses: online fill/success, away fill/warning, busy fill/critical, offline content/tertiary. The dot sits on the face's edge at 45° (inset = radius × 0.2929, so it sits on the circle, or on the squircle's rounded corner), with a ring of the surface colour (ring-colour, stroke/2). Dot sizes 6, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 by avatar size. The status is also in the accessible name; colour is never the only signal.
rules.group: A group overlaps faces by a set amount per size (4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14), each with a ring of the surface colour so the faces cut into each other. Later faces sit on top. Past max it shows one +N face (neutral tone, same size) and names the rest. The group is one unit: role group, labelled; each face keeps its name.
rules.light: A fallback face is a surface and is lit (D-020). A picture is media (data-media): it sits above the light, which dims to 25% while the pointer is over it.
rules.motion: A picture fades in at duration/fast; a status change fades at duration/fast (D-031). Nothing moves or resizes.
rules.a11y: A face is an image with the name as its accessible name (role img, aria-label), plus the status. Where the name is written next to the face, pass decorative: the face is then hidden from assistive tech and the name is not read twice. A +N face is named 'and N more'.
rules.interactive: An avatar is not a button. To make it one, wrap it in a Button or a link; the focus ring then belongs to that control.
rules.usage: Use an Avatar for a person, a brand or a workspace. For a count or a status label on its own use a Badge. A group of more than about five faces should show +N.

ring.$about: The cut-out ring around a status dot and between grouped faces.

tone.$about: Fallback fill, picked from the name.

badge.$about: Badge: a small, non-interactive label for a status, a count or a new-thing signal. Every value is a token reference, a plain even number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025). Unifies the editor Badge draft and the dashboard pills.
badge.title: Badge
badge.anatomy: One pill: [dot or icon] [label]. Three forms of the same frame: a label badge (text, optional leading dot or icon), a count badge (a number, 99+ above the cap) and a dot-only badge (no text, the 'new' signal on an icon or avatar). Height is not set: it is the line height of the label type plus padding y twice.

rules.role: Not interactive: no hover, no pressed, no focus, never a button. If it can be clicked, it is a Chip or a Button. It is a span with text; a dot-only badge is role img with an aria-label, because a dot alone says nothing to a screen reader.
rules.tones: Six tones: neutral, brand, success, warning, critical, info. Status tones mean what Status means in the rest of the system; brand is for what is new or yours, never for a plain status.
rules.variants: Soft is the default: fill/*-secondary with content/*, a tint that does not shout. Solid is the strong one: fill/* with content/on-*; neutral solid is fill/inverse with content/inverse-primary. Use solid for a count or a dot that must be seen on a busy surface, soft everywhere else.
rules.sizes: sm: label/sm (11/14) with padding y 2, so 18 tall. md: label/md (12/16) with padding y 4, so 24 tall. Heights come from padding, never from a typed height.
rules.radius: radius/full for every badge. A badge is a pill; a Chip is a squircle, so the two never read as the same thing.
rules.shade: Solid badges carry the inner shade (0, -4, blur 10, #000 50%), like any filled control. Soft badges are a tint and carry none; dot-only badges carry none. An effect, not a token (D-021).
rules.light: Label and count badges are lit (D-020). A dot-only badge is a signal, not a surface, and is not lit.
rules.icon: Lucide, in a frame from the icon scale: sm 12, md 16. The vector fills the key square of the icon grid.
rules.dot: A leading dot is 6, drawn in the tone's own colour (soft: fill/*, solid: the label colour). The dot-only badge is 8 (sm) or 10 (md).
rules.count: A number in tabular figures. One digit is a circle: min-width equals the height. Above the cap (default 99) it reads 99+. A count of 0 renders nothing. Give it a label ('unread') so a screen reader says what is being counted.
rules.anchor: On an icon, a button or an avatar the badge sits on the top-right corner, centred on it, with a ring of the surface colour (ring-colour, stroke/2) so it cuts out of what it covers. On a circle the corner is 14.6% in from each side, so the badge sits on the circle's edge. BadgeAnchor does this; the ring colour follows the surface the badge sits on.
rules.motion: A change of tone or variant fades at duration/fast (D-031). A badge that appears fades in; nothing slides or scales. Reduced motion keeps the fade.
rules.clip: A badge outside its anchor paints beyond the anchor's box, so a scrolling or clipping parent needs space for it (stroke/2 plus half the badge, D-037).
rules.usage: Use a Badge for a status (Live, Failed, Draft), a count on a nav item or icon, or a quiet 'New'. Do not use it for an action (Button), a removable or selectable tag (Chip), a message (Toast, Callout) or a long label: if it needs more than about two words, it is text.

ring.$about: The cut-out ring when a badge sits on another element.

soft.$about: Tint: fill/*-secondary, content/*. The dot is the vivid fill.

solid.$about: Strong: fill/*, content/on-*. The dot is the label colour.

button.$about: Button: every value is a token reference, 'none' or a rule (D-025, D-026). Status draft: the owner may still change it; it becomes stable when the owner says so.
button.anatomy: One frame: [icon] [label] [icon]. The frame carries height, padding x, gap, radius, fill and border; the same values apply to all three children. Either icon is optional; with no label the button is icon-only and square.

rules.height: size/control/{size}: 2xs 28, then 8px steps from xs 32 to 2xl 72. xs (32) is the everyday size. Fixed; children are centred, so padding y is not set: it is whatever is left over (2xs: 6).
rules.label: Text is always the body role, medium weight: 2xs 12, xs 14 (the everyday size), sm 14, md 16, lg 18, xl 20, 2xl 24. From md up, text stays about a third of the height.
rules.icon: A square frame from the icon scale, chosen by text size: 16 for 12 and 14px text, 20 for 16px, 24 for 18 and 20px, 32 for 24px. The vector follows the icon grid: it fills the key square (size/icon/grid/square, 75%).
rules.radius: Squircle: height × 0.375 (xs: 12 on 32), rounded to the nearest 4, so every size stays about equally round. 2xs sets its own: 10. Pill: radius/full (1000 in Figma). Same padding for both.
rules.states: Secondary, tertiary, outline and ghost: hover and pressed turn the icon content/brand; the label stays content/primary; the border stays in its own family, -hover on hover and -active when pressed (D-035). Brand, primary, brand-tone and brand-ghost change fill only.
rules.shade: Every state that has a fill gets the inner shade: inner shadow x 0, y −4, blur 10, spread 0, #000000 at 50%. No fill, no shade (outline, ghost and brand-ghost at rest; they get it on hover and press).
rules.grid: Every value you type in Figma is on the 4px grid; values under 12 may use 2px half-steps (2xs: padding x 10, radius 10). A plain number in a size means a set value that is not a token.

brand.about: The main action. One per view.

primary.about: Strong neutral action, light on dark.

tertiary.about: Quiet action; chips and settings in the prompt box.

ghost.about: No fill or border until hovered.

brand-tone.about: Brand action that should not shout.

brand-ghost.about: Brand text, fill only on hover.

button.linksAbout: Links have no frame: text (and an optional icon) in the button's label style for that size, no fill, no border, no padding. Colour changes per state.
button.loading: Disabled colours; the trailing icon becomes a spinner. The spinner is an icon: same frame, the ring fills the key square, line weight = frame × size/icon/grid/stroke.
button.focus: Rest colours plus a ring outside the border: border/focus, stroke/2.
button.effects: Inner shade on every filled state, inset 0 -4 10 rgba(0,0,0,.5). An effect, not a token (D-021).

checkbox.$about: Checkbox: a square well that holds a tick. Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025). Status draft: the owner may still change it.
checkbox.title: Checkbox
checkbox.anatomy: A row: [box] [label + description]. The box is a square well with a tick (checked) or a dash (indeterminate) drawn as an icon inside it. The whole row is the click target. A group is a column or a row of these rows under a group label.

rules.states: Unchecked, checked, indeterminate; each at rest, hover, pressed, focus and disabled. Unchecked is a well: fill/primary with border/secondary. Checked and indeterminate look the same: fill/inverse (white, like shadcn's primary, D-038) with a content/inverse-primary mark. Orange stays for the one main action (D-003).
rules.hover: Hover is the -hover fill and border of the box's own family (D-035). Pressed is one step stronger, the -active fill and border. Hover and press work on the whole row, label included. Nothing moves or changes size: the border is an inset box-shadow.
rules.shade: No inner shade, unlike Button: at 16–20px the shade greys the white out, so on stays a flat, solid fill that pops (D-041). The box is a lit surface (D-020).
rules.mark: The mark is drawn for the box, not taken from the icon set: a tick about 7/16 of the box wide and a 6/16 dash, both with a 2/16 stroke (2px in the 16 box, 2.5px in the 20) and round caps. A full-size icon tick read too big and too thin. It draws in from the left while it fades (duration/base, easing/standard) and fades out the same way. Check and dash swap by drawing one out and the other in. Reduced motion: the fade stays, the draw goes (D-031).
rules.size: sm: box 16 (size/icon/sm), radius xs. md: box 20 (size/icon/md), radius sm. md is the default. Text is the same in both: label body/md/regular, description body/sm/regular.
rules.colours: Label content/primary, description content/tertiary. Disabled: label content/primary-disabled, description content/tertiary-disabled, box -disabled fill and border; a disabled checked box uses fill/secondary-disabled and a content/primary-disabled mark, like a disabled primary Button, because fill/inverse-disabled is the same grey as its mark.
rules.focus: Keyboard focus (focus-visible only) draws a ring outside the box: border/focus, stroke/2. The row never clips it. A scroll or clip container around a checkbox keeps stroke/2 of room (D-037).
rules.hit: The visible box is smaller than size/target (44). An invisible layer around the box makes the hit area at least 44 x 44 without moving anything. The label and description are part of the click target too.
rules.keyboard: Tab reaches each checkbox. Space toggles it. Enter does not (that submits a form). A disabled checkbox leaves the Tab order.
rules.aria: A native input type=checkbox, so form, label and mixed state work as usual. The label names it (aria-labelledby), the description describes it (aria-describedby). Indeterminate is the input's own indeterminate state (aria-checked mixed). With no visible label, pass aria-label. A group is role=group named by its group label.
rules.indeterminate: Mixed state for a parent that controls a list: some of the children are checked. Clicking it checks it (the parent decides what the children do). It is a display state, never something a user sets on a single option.
rules.group: A group label (body/md/medium, content/primary), then the options. Vertical: space/12 between options. Horizontal: space/24. The group label sits space/8 above the options. A disabled group disables every option.
rules.use: Use a checkbox when each option is independent and zero, one or many can be on, or for one explicit agreement. Use a Switch when the change takes effect at once. Use Radio when exactly one of several must be chosen.
rules.light: The box is lit by light/cursor (D-020). The label is plain text and is not.

box.$about: The square. sm and md are icon frames.

unchecked.$about: A well: darker than the surface it sits on.

checked.$about: Checked and indeterminate: the 'on' colour, white (D-038).

chip.$about: Chip: a compact interactive control: a filter, a choice, an input or a setting. Built from the settings chips in Home's prompt box. Every value is a token reference, a plain even number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025).
chip.title: Chip
chip.anatomy: One frame: [check or icon or image] [label] [trailing icon or remove button]. Fixed height from size/control, so children are centred and padding y is not set. Four kinds share it: action (a setting that opens or does something), filter (toggles on and off), choice (one of a group, with a sliding indicator) and input (a value you can remove).

rules.kinds: Action: a plain button, optionally with a menu or a trailing icon. Filter: aria-pressed, toggles on click, Space and Enter. Choice: role radio in a radiogroup, one selected, arrow keys move. Input: a value the user added; the trailing cross Button removes it.
rules.sizes: Two sizes on the Button scale: xs 32 (the everyday size, the Home prompt box) and 2xs 28. Label is label/md/medium at xs (12/16, as Home) and label/sm/medium at 2xs (11/14). The icon frame is size/icon/sm (16) in both.
rules.radius: Squircle like Button: xs radius/lg (12), 2xs 10 (set, like Button 2xs). Nesting: the remove Button is a 2xs Button (28, radius 10); inside an xs chip it sits 2 from the end, and 2 + 10 = 12 keeps the corners parallel. Inside a 2xs chip it fills the end.
rules.states: Rest, hover, pressed, selected, disabled, plus a focus ring. Hover: fill/tertiary-hover, border/tertiary-hover, icon content/brand (as the Button tertiary type). Pressed: fill/tertiary-active, border/tertiary-active, icon content/brand (D-035). Selected is the pressed look held: the -active fill and border, icon content/brand, plus a check where there is no leading icon. Hover on a selected chip keeps the selected look. Choice chips in a group rest as outlines (no fill, border/tertiary) so the indicator can be seen sliding under them; the chosen one takes the selected look. Disabled uses the -disabled fill and border and content/primary-disabled.
rules.border: Always stroke/1 and inset, drawn as a box-shadow, so nothing moves or changes size on hover or press (D-035).
rules.shade: The inner shade (0, -4, blur 10, #000 50%) on every state that has a fill (not the outlined choice rest). An effect, not a token (D-021).
rules.light: A chip is lit (D-020). A leading image or logo is media (data-media) and sits above the light.
rules.focus: A ring outside the border: border/focus, stroke/2, drawn on focus-visible only. The container keeps stroke/2 of room on every side, so the ring is never clipped (D-037).
rules.swap: A trailing icon can swap to another on hover and focus: Home's tool chip shows a double chevron that becomes a cross. The two icons crossfade and slide 4px at duration/base, easing/standard (motion-swap, D-031). The swap is a hint on the chip; it is not a separate button.
rules.check: A filter chip with no leading icon shows a 16 check when selected. It grows in from zero width and fades at duration/fast, so the label does not jump. With a leading icon or image there is no check: the icon turns content/brand.
rules.indicator: A choice group has one indicator, a chip surface in the selected look, that slides from the old chip to the new one: position and size together, duration/base, easing/standard, the same time at any distance, in a straight line along a row, a column or a grid (D-032). The chosen chip paints no fill of its own, so nothing flashes. The first paint never animates. Hover and press on the chosen chip style the indicator once it has landed. Reduced motion: a cross-fade.
rules.keyboard: Tab reaches every chip. Space and Enter press an action chip and toggle a filter chip. In a choice group Tab stops once, on the chosen chip (roving tabindex); arrow keys move and choose, Home and End jump. On an input chip Backspace and Delete remove it; the cross Button is for the mouse and touch, so it is out of the Tab order and the chip is one stop. After removing, focus moves to the next chip, or the previous one.
rules.aria: Action: a button. Filter: a button with aria-pressed. Choice: a radiogroup with radio chips (aria-checked). Input: a group labelled with its text and aria-keyshortcuts Backspace Delete; its cross Button is named 'Remove <label>'. A chip with only an icon needs a label. Disabled chips stay in the DOM and keep their place.
rules.motion: Every state change (fill, border, icon colour, shadow) fades at duration/fast (D-031). Reduced motion keeps the fades and drops the slides.
rules.usage: Use a Chip for a compact setting, a filter, one choice among a few short options, or a value the user typed or picked. Use a Button for an action on the page, a Segmented control for a mode that reads as a tool switch, a Badge for a status that is not clickable, a Menu or Select for more than about six options.

xs.$about: Everyday size, the Home prompt box.

2xs.$about: Compact. Radius and padding set by hand, like Button 2xs.

image.$about: A leading logo or picture, in the icon frame.

dialog.$about: Dialog: a modal that asks for one thing or tells one thing and blocks the page until it is answered. Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule. This spec is the authority (D-025).
dialog.title: Dialog
dialog.anatomy: A scrim over the page, then one panel: header (title, optional description, close button), a scrolling body, a footer with the actions. Three widths (sm, md, lg). Alert dialog: the same panel with no close button, a short message and two actions. Below 640 the panel is a bottom sheet: full width, anchored to the bottom edge, top corners rounded.

rules.use: Use a dialog when the answer must come before anything else happens: a short form, a confirmation, a choice that is hard to undo. Do not use it for a message that needs no answer (use a toast), for help text on one control (use a tooltip or popover), for a menu or a pick from a list (use a menu or select), or for anything the person may want to look at while working (use a panel in the page).
rules.variants: Dialog (role dialog) and alert dialog (role alertdialog). The alert dialog has no close button, does not close on a scrim press, is sm wide, and is for one question: confirm or cancel. When the confirm action is destructive the focus starts on Cancel, never on the destructive action.
rules.size: sm 400, md 520, lg 640. The panel is never wider than the window minus 2 x panel.inset. Height follows the content up to the window height minus 2 x panel.inset (100dvh); beyond that only the body scrolls.
rules.layout: Panel: surface/primary, border/primary, radius/2xl, the inner shade (0, -4, blur 10, #000 50%), the same panel as the search dialog, so there is one modal look. Header: title (heading/sm/semibold) and the close button on one line, 32 tall; the description (body/md/regular, content/secondary) sits under the title. The text starts 24 from the left edge. Body: body/md/regular. Footer: actions on the right, gap 8; an optional note or checkbox on the left. Order: the safe action first, the main action last.
rules.actions: At most one brand Button per dialog (D-026). The main action is a brand Button; a dialog whose answer is a plain yes uses primary (white). Cancel is ghost. Other actions are secondary. Buttons are size sm (40), size md (48) in the sheet so every target is at least 44. A destructive confirm has no Button type of its own: it is a secondary Button with the label and icon in content/critical (hover content/critical-hover, pressed content/critical-active). Proposal: a critical Button type.
rules.scrim: color-mix of background at 72% and transparent, with a backdrop blur of scrim.blur (space/4): the same values as the search dialog. 72% is a set value, not a token (D-021). The scrim fades in at duration/base and out at duration/fast (motion-fade). A press (pointerdown) on the scrim closes the dialog unless the dialog is blocking or scrimClose is off; a press inside the panel that ends on the scrim does not.
rules.motion: Enter: the scrim fades; the panel fades, drops 4px and scales from 0.98 at duration/base, easing/enter (motion-pop, origin centre). Leave: both fade at duration/fast, easing/exit; the panel stays mounted until the fade ends (usePresence). Sheet: enters by sliding up from its own height at duration/slow, easing/enter, and leaves with the fade. Reduced motion keeps every fade and drops the scale, the drop and the slide (D-031).
rules.focus: On open, focus moves into the panel: the first field in the body, else the main action in the footer (the safe action in an alert dialog whose confirm is destructive), else the panel itself (tabindex -1). The close button is never the first stop. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside the panel; focus that escapes (a click on the page, a script) is pulled back. On close, focus returns to the element that had it when the dialog opened, or to a trigger passed in. Focus rings are never clipped: header and footer keep their padding, the body keeps panel.body.padding-y and padding-x, both larger than stroke/2 (D-037).
rules.keyboard: Esc closes (unless blocking), but only when no layer inside the dialog (a select, a menu) already handled it (event.defaultPrevented). Tab and Shift+Tab cycle. Space and Enter activate the focused Button. Only the topmost of stacked dialogs answers Esc and traps focus.
rules.aria: role dialog or alertdialog, aria-modal true, aria-labelledby the title, aria-describedby the description (alert dialog: the description is required, it is the question). The close button has aria-label Close. The panel is the only thing reading as interactive while open: nothing behind it takes focus. The scrim is not focusable and has no role.
rules.scroll: The page does not scroll while a dialog is open: html gets overflow hidden and, only when the page has a scrollbar, scrollbar-gutter stable, so the page never shifts sideways. Only the body scrolls, with overscroll-behavior contain, so the scroll never passes to the page. Pop-ups show no scroll bar: instead a blurred fade of fade.height (space/24) sits on the top edge once the body is scrolled and on the bottom edge while more is below, in surface/primary with a backdrop blur of fade.blur. Header and footer never scroll away.
rules.sheet: Below 640 (container width, so a specimen in a 360 frame behaves like a phone): the panel is full width, bottom-aligned with no side or bottom gap, radius/2xl on the top corners only, max height 85% of the window, and the footer clears the device's bottom safe area. The actions share the footer row equally. The close button grows to size/control/sm (40). There is no drag handle, because the sheet is not draggable: it closes with Close, Esc, a scrim press or an action.
rules.blocking: A blocking dialog ignores Esc and scrim presses and has no close button, so only its actions end it. Use it only while work is running that must not be interrupted. It still traps focus and still has a title.
rules.layers: z-index 1040: above the page and the side nav, below the search dialog (1050) and the toaster (1070), so a toast fired from a dialog stays visible. The overlay is a light root (data-light-root): the panel is a lit surface (D-020).
rules.static: A specimen for the docs only: the panel without the scrim, the portal, the trap, the scroll lock or the keys. It is inert, so it leaves the Tab order.
rules.states: Actions use the Button states. The panel itself has none. Loading is the Button's: the confirm shows the spinner and the dialog stays open until the work ends.

scrim.$about: Over the whole window. Colour is background at 72% (set value in CSS, shared with the search dialog); blur is this token.

panel.$about: The dialog surface. Width is by size; inset is the least gap to the window edge (none in the sheet).

header.$about: Title row (32 tall, the close button's height) and the description under it.

body.$about: The scrolling area. Its padding is also the clip room for focus rings (D-037, more than stroke/2 on every side).

fade.$about: The soft edge that shows the body can scroll (no scroll bar in pop-ups).

footer.$about: The actions, right-aligned. Buttons are size sm (40); the sheet uses md (48), at least the 44 touch target.

sheet.$about: Below this container width the panel is a bottom sheet. Keep equal to the container query in dialog.css.

critical.$about: Label and icon of a destructive confirm Button (secondary Button, content/critical).

menu.$about: Menu: a dropdown opened from a trigger (any Button). Also the surface and the item look that Select builds on. Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025).
menu.title: Menu
menu.anatomy: A floating surface (a light root) holding one scrolling list. The list holds items, group labels and separators. An item is: leading mark or icon, label (+ description), then a shortcut or a submenu chevron. One highlight indicator sits behind the items and slides to the one pointed at or reached by keyboard. A submenu is a second surface beside its parent item (one level).

rules.when: Use a Menu for a list of actions or settings behind one trigger (more, account, view options). Use Select to choose one value for a field. Use Segmented when 2 to 4 options must stay visible. Never put a form field or a long page of content in a menu.
rules.trigger: Any Button (or any control). The trigger gets aria-haspopup='menu', aria-expanded and aria-controls from the Menu. It stays pressed (state active) while the menu is open.
rules.tier: The surface is surface/tertiary, the tier of floating cards (D-036), with border/tertiary and the inner shade, exactly like Home's brand menu. surface/secondary is the tooltip tier and is not used here. Items sit on the surface, so the highlight is fill/tertiary-hover, one step lighter.
rules.sheen: The surface carries the four soft blobs of Home's brand menu: content/primary, 10% opacity, a 38px blur (Figma blur 75), clipped to the surface and above the items, pointer-events none. A Figma effect, not a token (D-021).
rules.light: The surface is a <Light> root (D-020): it carries its own light wherever it opens. A submenu is its own light root.
rules.highlight: One indicator (D-032), not a style on each item. It is a rounded fill with an inset border and the inner shade, so nothing moves. It slides from the old item to the new one, position and size together, duration/base, easing/standard, whatever the distance. The first time it shows, and the first time after the pointer has left, it appears in place and fades in (duration/fast): it never slides in from a stale spot. Rest of the time without a highlighted item it is hidden (opacity 0, duration/fast). Hover: fill/tertiary-hover and border/tertiary-hover. Pressed: fill/tertiary-active and border/tertiary-active (D-035), shown only once the indicator has landed. Reached by keyboard it also draws the focus ring, border/focus, inset stroke/2, so it can never be clipped. Reduced motion: no slide, the indicator cross-fades.
rules.items: Four kinds: action (menuitem), checkbox (menuitemcheckbox, a check mark when checked), radio (menuitemradio, a dot when checked; one per group), submenu (an item with items, trailing chevron-right). Checkable items keep a leading mark slot, so labels line up whether or not they are checked. A description sits under the label. A shortcut is shown as text on the right (content/tertiary); it only labels the key, the app binds it. An action closes the menu after it runs; checkbox and radio items close it too unless the item says keepOpen.
rules.danger: A danger item (delete, remove) uses content/critical for its text and icon. It uses the same highlight. Put it last, after a separator.
rules.disabled: A disabled item uses the -disabled content tokens, is skipped by arrow keys and typeahead, never takes the highlight and never runs. It stays in place so nothing shifts. aria-disabled is set.
rules.groups: A group label (label/sm/medium, content/tertiary) names the items below it, inside role='group' with aria-labelledby. A separator (border/elevated, stroke/1) splits kinds of items. Use either, not both in a row.
rules.submenu: One level. It opens beside the parent item (after duration/fast of hover, on click, Enter, Space or ArrowRight), top-aligned with the item, and flips to the left when the right side has no room. The parent item keeps the highlight and aria-expanded while it is open. ArrowLeft or Esc closes it and returns focus to the parent item. Selecting a submenu item closes every level. Moving the pointer to another item of the parent closes it after the same delay.
rules.placement: Below the trigger (default), aligned to its start edge, surface.offset away. It flips above when below is too short and above is longer, and ends up inside the viewport, surface.viewport-margin from every edge. Align end puts the right edges together. Width fits the content between surface.min-width and surface.max-width. It repositions on scroll and resize.
rules.scroll: Height is at most surface.max-height and what the viewport leaves. Taller content scrolls inside the surface, never the page (overscroll contain), with the one scrollbar (D-037). The scroll area keeps stroke/2 of room on every side (padding, pulled back by a matching negative margin) so the focus ring and the indicator border are never cut.
rules.keyboard: On the trigger: Enter, Space and ArrowDown open the menu and focus the first item; ArrowUp opens it and focuses the last. In the menu: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move (wrapping), Home and End jump, ArrowRight opens a submenu, ArrowLeft closes one, Enter and Space run the item, a letter jumps to the next item whose label starts with what you typed (the typed text resets after 500 ms), Esc closes and returns focus to the trigger, Tab closes and moves on from the trigger. A click on the trigger opens the menu with no item focused, so no highlight shows until you point at one or press a key.
rules.pointer: Pointing at an item focuses it and moves the highlight. Clicking outside the menu and its submenu closes it, and the press is not passed on as a selection. Leaving the list hides the highlight.
rules.aria: Surface role='menu' (aria-orientation vertical) labelled by the trigger. Items as above. The trigger names the menu. Icons are decorative (aria-hidden). Focus moves onto the item (roving), so screen readers read it.
rules.motion: The surface enters with motion-pop from the side it opens on (fade, 4px drop, scale from 0.98, duration/base, easing/enter) and leaves with a fade (duration/fast, easing/exit), kept mounted by usePresence. Every state change runs at duration/fast (D-031). Reduced motion keeps the fades and drops the drop and the scale.
rules.select: Select (components/select.json) reuses this surface, list and item look. Its options are items with role='option', the check sits at the end, and it matches the trigger's width.

surface.$about: The floating card. A light root. offset: gap to the trigger. offset-attached: the gap when the surface belongs to a field (Select). sub-offset: gap to the parent surface. min-width and max-width: menu width limits; max-height: the tallest it grows before it scrolls. scroll-room: clip room for focus rings (D-037).

sheen.$about: Home's four soft blobs (content/primary at 10% opacity). Set sizes, not tokens (D-021).

item.$about: 32 tall (6 + 20 + 6). Radius lg (12) inside a 4 padding gives the surface's xl (16) corner: inner + padding = outer. With a description it grows to fit.

hover.$about: The indicator when the pointer or the keyboard is on an item. The icon turns content/primary.

pressed.$about: The indicator while the item is pressed (D-035).

focus.$about: Keyboard focus: an inset ring on the indicator, stroke/2.

popover.$about: Popover: an anchored, non-modal floating panel with any content, opened by a click on its trigger. For a list of commands use a Menu; for a question that blocks the page use a Dialog. Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-002, D-025).
popover.title: Popover
popover.anatomy: A floating card beside its trigger: an optional header (title on the left, a ghost close Button on the right), a body with any content, and an optional footer of actions aligned to the right. The page behind stays usable.

rules.use: Use it for a small task or a detail that belongs to one control: a setting group, an export panel, a share box, a colour picker. Not for a list of commands (Menu), not for a one-line label (Tooltip), and not when the user must answer before going on (Dialog). Keep it to one task; if it needs a lot of scrolling, it wants a page or a sheet.
rules.surface: surface/tertiary, border/tertiary, radius/xl, inner shade and drop shadow (D-021): the floating-card tier of D-036, which is what the editor's popovers and Home's menus already use. Tertiary is one step above the secondary panels and cards it opens from, so it reads as raised without a heavier shadow. It is a light root (<Light>, D-020): it carries its own light wherever it opens. Inside, wells go darker (fill/primary) and raised things lighter, as in D-036.
rules.layout: A column. Padding 16 (space/16), gap 12 (space/12) between header, body and footer. No dividers: space tells the parts apart (D-036). Header: the title in heading/xs/semibold, content/primary; the close button is a ghost Button, size 2xs, icon x, label Close. Body: body/md/regular, content/secondary; it brings its own controls and colours. Footer: right-aligned Buttons, size xs, 8 apart, wrapping when narrow; the one main action is primary or brand (one brand fill per view), the other is ghost or secondary. Header and footer are optional; with no title, give the popover a label (aria-label).
rules.sizes: Three fixed widths: sm 240, md 320 (default), lg 400, all set values. The width never depends on where the popover sits. It never exceeds the window minus 8 on each side. Height follows the content up to the window height minus 16; past that the body scrolls (header and footer stay) with the one minimal scrollbar (D-037), and keeps a stroke/2 margin for focus rings so they are never clipped.
rules.placement: bottom (default), top, left, right, with align start (default), center or end along the trigger's edge. 8 from the trigger (space/8). It flips to the opposite side when the preferred side has no room and the other has; if neither fits it takes the side with more room. It is then clamped 8 inside the window on every side. It follows the trigger while the page scrolls or resizes. position: fixed in a portal on the document: no scroll container clips it and no lit surface traps it beneath another layer. Layer z-index 1080 (set value), below tooltips.
rules.open: A click (or Enter / Space) on the trigger toggles it. Esc, a press outside, a focus move outside, the close button and any action that calls close() shut it. One Esc closes one popover: the newest (nested popovers close from the inside out). Controlled (open, onOpenChange) or not (defaultOpen).
rules.focus: Opened by keyboard: focus moves into the popover, to the element marked data-autofocus, else the first control of the body or footer, else the panel itself. Opened by pointer: focus stays on the trigger (the pointer user has not asked for focus to move), and Tab from the trigger goes into the popover. Tab at the end of the popover leaves it for whatever follows the trigger in the page, and Shift+Tab at the start goes back to the trigger, so a non-modal popover never traps focus. Focus returns to the trigger when it closes by Esc, close button or action; it does not when the user pressed or tabbed somewhere else. A popover that starts open (defaultOpen) does not take focus.
rules.aria: The trigger gets aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-expanded (true while open) and aria-controls (the panel's id, while open). The panel is role=dialog (not aria-modal: the page stays usable), named by aria-labelledby (the title) or, with no title, aria-label.
rules.motion: Enter: fade, a 4 slide towards its final place from the trigger's side, scale from 0.98 from the corner it grows from: duration/base, easing/enter (motion-pop, D-031). Left and right placements fade and scale only. Leave: fade, duration/fast, easing/exit; it stays mounted until it has faded (usePresence) and ignores the pointer while it does. Reduced motion keeps the fade and drops the movement.
rules.api: <Popover trigger={<Button>Export</Button>} title="Export" size="md" placement="bottom" align="start" footer={...}>body</Popover>. trigger is one element that accepts a ref and onClick (a Button, or a Tooltip wrapping one, which passes them on). children and footer may be functions of { close }. Other props: label, closable (false hides the close button), open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange. PopoverPanel draws the same panel inline, for documentation specimens.
rules.migrate: The editor's popovers (Popovers.jsx, .ed-pop) become <Popover>; so do the panel-style popups in Home's Menus.jsx. Menus of commands wait for the Menu component.

panel.$about: The card. Widths 240 / 320 / 400 are set values.

header.$about: Title and close button. As tall as a 2xs Button.

progress.$about: Progress: a linear bar and a ring (the spinner). Every value is a token reference, a plain even number (a set value in px, not a token) or a rule (D-025). Draft: the owner may still change it.
progress.title: Progress
progress.anatomy: Bar: an optional head row (label left, value right) over a track with one filled part. Ring: a square icon frame (the Spinner) with an arc inside it. The ring is an icon (D-028): the same frame as every icon, the ring fills the key square (size/icon/grid/square, 75% of the frame) and its line weight is frame x size/icon/grid/stroke (1/16). Determinate or indeterminate, for both.

rules.choose: Bar: work with a known end that takes longer than about 2 seconds and has a place of its own (an upload, a render, a step in a flow). Ring: work with no known end, or a place too small for a bar (inside a button, next to a label, a block waiting for its data). Skeleton: the shape of the content is known and it will fill in. There is no skeleton component yet; until there is one, use a ring for a short wait and a bar for a long one. Under about 400 ms show nothing: a flash of progress reads as slower than none.
rules.aria: The bar is role=progressbar with aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax 100, aria-valuenow (rounded) and aria-valuetext when the text says more than the percentage. Indeterminate: aria-valuenow is left out, which is how a screen reader hears "busy, no value". It is named by its label (aria-labelledby) or by aria-label. aria-busy is true until the value reaches 100; the region being loaded should carry aria-busy too. The ring is role=progressbar with the same rules and the accessible name "Loading" unless you pass a label. Inside a Button, the button already says busy (aria-busy) and the ring there is decoration.
rules.sizes: Bar heights are set values, 2, 4 and 8, not tokens: stroke tokens stop at 2 and space tokens are for gaps. 2 (sm) is a hairline under a header or on a card edge; 4 (md) is the everyday bar; 8 (lg) is for a bar that is the content of its place, such as an upload row. Ring sizes are the icon scale: xs 12, sm 16, md 20, lg 24, xl 32 (D-022).
rules.tones: Neutral (default): fill/inverse, the primary look (D-038); progress is status, not the one main action. Brand: fill/brand, only when the progress is the main event of the screen (the one orange thing). Success: fill/success, for a finished or healthy state. Critical: fill/critical, for a failed one. The track never changes: fill/tertiary on a bar, fill/tertiary-active on a ring (its line is thin, so it needs one step more).
rules.determinate: Changes in value animate: the filled width follows at duration/base, easing/standard (D-031). The first paint never animates. The value is clamped to 0 to 100. Reduced motion drops the movement: the bar jumps.
rules.indeterminate: A segment 40% of the track wide travels from before the start to after the end, 1.4s per pass, easing/standard, repeating. Reduced motion: no travel; the whole bar pulses slowly between 40% and 100% opacity (2.4s).
rules.shade: The inner shade (0, -4, blur 10, #000 50%) goes on the 8 bar's filled part. At 2 and 4 it would fill the whole bar, so those have none. The ring has none (it is a line, like an icon).
rules.light: A bar is a thin indicator, not a surface: it is not lit.
rules.ring: An SVG in the icon frame. The arc is round-capped like the HeyOz icon set. Indeterminate: a 3/4 arc turning once every 0.8s, linear. Reduced motion: 2.4s (still turns, so it still reads as busy). Determinate: the arc starts at 12 o'clock and grows clockwise; the filled length follows the value at duration/base. The colour is the tone, or the surrounding text colour with tone inherit.
rules.label: The head row is label/md/medium: the label in content/primary, the value in content/secondary with tabular figures, so the number does not jiggle. The value is hidden from screen readers (the bar already announces it).
rules.grid: Set values are on the 4px grid with 2px half-steps (D-025). Loop times are set values and not tokens: 0.8s and 2.4s for the ring, 1.4s and 2.4s for the bar (the same set values as the button spinner).

head.$about: The label row above a bar.

bar.$about: The track and its filled part.

ring.$about: The spinner: icon frames, one per icon size.

tone.$about: The colour of the filled part (bar) and of the arc (ring).

radio.$about: Radio: a round well with a dot. One option of several. Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025). Status draft: the owner may still change it.
radio.title: Radio
radio.anatomy: A radio group is a column or a row of radios under an optional group label. A radio is a row: [circle] [label + description]. The circle is a round well; the chosen one holds a dot. The whole row is the click target.

rules.states: Unchecked, checked; each at rest, hover, pressed, focus and disabled. Unchecked is a well: fill/primary with border/secondary. Checked is fill/inverse (white, like shadcn's primary, D-038) with a content/inverse-primary dot. Orange stays for the one main action (D-003).
rules.hover: Hover is the -hover fill and border of the circle's own family (D-035). Pressed is one step stronger, the -active fill and border. Hover and press work on the whole row, label included. Nothing moves or changes size: the border is an inset box-shadow.
rules.shade: No inner shade, unlike Button: at 16–20px the shade greys the white out, so on stays a flat, solid fill that pops (D-041). The circle is a lit surface (D-020).
rules.dot: The dot is a set value: 6 in the sm circle, 8 in the md circle. It grows from 50% to full size while it fades in, and fades out when another radio is chosen (duration/base, easing/standard). Reduced motion: the fade stays, the growth goes (D-031).
rules.size: sm: circle 16 (size/icon/sm). md: circle 20 (size/icon/md). md is the default. Text is the same in both: label body/md/regular, description body/sm/regular.
rules.colours: Label content/primary, description content/tertiary. Disabled: label content/primary-disabled, description content/tertiary-disabled, circle -disabled fill and border; a disabled checked circle uses fill/secondary-disabled and a content/primary-disabled dot, like a disabled primary Button, because fill/inverse-disabled is the same grey as its dot.
rules.focus: Keyboard focus (focus-visible only) draws a ring outside the circle: border/focus, stroke/2. The row never clips it. A scroll or clip container around a group keeps stroke/2 of room (D-037).
rules.hit: The visible circle is smaller than size/target (44). An invisible layer around the circle makes the hit area at least 44 x 44 without moving anything. The label and description are part of the click target too.
rules.keyboard: Roving tabindex: the group is one Tab stop. Tab lands on the chosen radio, or on the first enabled one when none is chosen. Arrow Down and Right move to the next radio and choose it; Up and Left go back; both wrap round the ends. Home and End go to the first and the last enabled radio and choose it. Space chooses the focused radio. Disabled radios are skipped by the arrows and are not in the Tab order.
rules.aria: The group is role=radiogroup named by its group label (aria-labelledby), or by aria-label. Each radio is role=radio with aria-checked, named by its label (aria-labelledby) and described by its description (aria-describedby). Disabled radios carry aria-disabled.
rules.group: A group label (body/md/medium, content/primary), then the options. Vertical: space/12 between options. Horizontal: space/24. The group label sits space/8 above the options. A disabled group disables every option. With no default, none is chosen.
rules.use: Use a radio group when exactly one of two to five options must be chosen and all of them should be visible. Use Select for more than five. Use Segmented for a view or mode that changes the screen at once. Use a Switch for a single on/off. Clicking the chosen radio again does not clear it; offer a 'None' option when that is needed.
rules.light: The circle is lit by light/cursor (D-020). The label is plain text and is not.

circle.$about: The round well. sm and md are icon frames.

dot.$about: The chosen mark: a set value, not a token.

unchecked.$about: A well: darker than the surface it sits on.

checked.$about: The chosen radio: the 'on' colour, white (D-038).

segmented.$about: Segmented control: pick one value from a short list that is always visible. Built from Button (the options) and one sliding indicator (D-032). Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025).
segmented.title: Segmented
segmented.anatomy: A frame holding 2 to 6 options in a row (or a grid, or a column). Each option is a Button of the frame's size: a label, an icon, or an icon and a label. One indicator sits behind the chosen option and slides to the next one.

rules.use: Segmented sets a value: unit, alignment, speed, framing, resolution. The options are the whole answer, all visible, one always chosen. To switch between views of content (a page, a list, a panel), use Tabs. For more than 6 options, or long labels, use Select.
rules.sizes: The sizes are Button's: 2xs 28, xs 32 (the everyday size), sm 40, md 48, lg 56, xl 64, 2xl 72. Every option is a Button of that size, so its height, label, icon frame and padding come from Button's spec. The frame adds the padding below on top.
rules.radius: Nesting rule: frame radius = the option's Button radius (squircle, Button's rule) + frame padding, so inner and outer corners stay parallel. xs: 12 + 4 = 16.
rules.options: Label only, icon only, or icon and label. An icon-only option is square (the size's height) and needs an accessible name, passed as label. Pass the options as [value, label, extra]: extra is { icon, label, off }.
rules.indicator: One element behind the chosen option: a real tertiary Button surface (fill/tertiary, border/tertiary, inner shade, D-021). It is not a style on each option. The chosen option paints no fill of its own, so nothing flashes. Until the indicator is placed (first paint, no JavaScript), the chosen option wears the same tertiary look itself.
rules.states: Option: rest (ghost Button), hover, pressed, disabled, chosen. Hover and pressed on a ghost option are Button's: fill, an inset border in its own family (border/secondary-hover, then border/secondary-active, D-035) and the icon turning content/brand. Hover and pressed on the chosen option style the indicator (tertiary hover, tertiary pressed), but only once it has landed: while it travels it keeps the plain chosen look (D-032). Nothing moves or changes size on hover.
rules.disabled: A disabled option stays in place, dimmed, and cannot be chosen or focused by arrow keys. The group keeps its size, so nothing shifts. Never remove an option that does not apply; disable it.
rules.width: Fill (default): the frame is as wide as its container and the options share it equally (grid columns of 1fr). Hug (fit): the frame is as wide as its options, each option as wide as its own content, icon-only options square. Pass cols for a grid, for example 2 columns of 2, or 1 for a column.
rules.motion: The indicator slides from the old option to the new one: position and size together, duration/base, easing/standard, in a straight line, the same duration whatever the distance (D-032). Labels change colour in place at duration/fast (D-031). The first paint never animates. Reduced motion: no slide, a cross-fade.
rules.keyboard: role radiogroup with role radio options (aria-checked). One Tab stop for the group: the chosen option (the first enabled one if none is chosen). Arrow keys (left or up = previous, right or down = next) move focus and choose, skipping disabled options and wrapping at the ends. Home and End go to the first and last enabled option. Space and Enter choose the focused option. The frame carries aria-label (label).
rules.focus: A stroke/2 ring in border/focus around the focused option, drawn outside it. The frame is not a clipping container, so the ring is never cut; inside the frame the padding (4) is larger than the ring (2).
rules.light: The frame is a lit surface above the background (D-020), and so are the options (Button). The inner shade sits on the frame and on filled options (D-021).

frame.$about: The track the options sit in.

indicator.$about: A tertiary Button surface: these are Button's tertiary values (components/button.json), read here so the component is whole in one place. The indicator paints them.

select.$about: Select: choose one value from a list, in a form. The trigger looks like a text field; the list is the Menu's surface and item look (components/menu.json). Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025).
select.title: Select
select.anatomy: A field: label above, the trigger (well with an optional icon, the value or placeholder, a chevron), then a hint or an error below. Pressing the trigger opens a listbox under it, as wide as the trigger. The chosen option shows a check at its end.

rules.when: Use Select to pick one value from 4 to about 12 options in a form. Use Segmented for 2 to 4 options that should stay visible. Use Menu for actions. Over about 12 options a list needs search, which Select does not have yet.
rules.fieldConventions: Shared with the text field so they sit side by side. Heights on size/control: xs 32 (everyday), sm 40, md 48. Radius: xs radius/lg, sm radius/xl, md radius/2xl. Padding x as Button for the size: xs space/12, sm space/16, md space/20. Value body/md/regular (xs, sm) and body/lg/regular (md). Label label/md/medium content/secondary, gap space/6 to the well. Hint and error body/sm/regular, gap space/6.
rules.well: Fill fill/primary and border border/primary, an inset border so nothing moves. Hover: fill/primary-hover and border/primary-hover. Open and focus: fill/primary and border/primary-active; no ring (subtle, like the text field). Disabled: fill/primary-disabled, border/primary-disabled, text content/primary-disabled. All changes run at duration/fast (D-031). The well carries the inner shade, like the text field's.
rules.value: The chosen label in content/primary. With nothing chosen, the placeholder in content/tertiary. A long label is cut with an ellipsis, never wrapped. The chosen option's icon shows in the well before the label, content/secondary.
rules.invalid: Invalid: border/critical (hover border/critical-hover, open border/critical-active), the message below in content/critical with aria-describedby and aria-invalid on the trigger. The message starts with a circle-alert icon (size/icon/xs) and replaces the hint, in the same space.
rules.chevron: chevron-down, size/icon/sm, content/secondary, at the end of the well. On open it turns over: chevron-down fades out and turns 180 degrees while chevron-up turns in and fades in, duration/base, easing/standard (D-031). Reduced motion: the fade stays, the turn goes.
rules.surface: The list is the Menu's surface (surface/tertiary: floating card tier, D-036; border/tertiary; inner shade; sheen; a light root), placed below the trigger with offset-attached (space/4) between. It flips above when below is too short, and stays inside the viewport. Width is the trigger's width, never narrower; longer labels are cut with an ellipsis. Height is at most menu surface.max-height, then it scrolls inside with the one scrollbar and stroke/2 of clip room (D-037). It enters with motion-pop and leaves with a fade (usePresence).
rules.options: An option has a label and optionally an icon (Lucide) and a description. A group label and a separator are allowed. A disabled option shows the -disabled colours, is skipped by arrows and typeahead and cannot be chosen. The chosen option shows a check (check, size/icon/sm) at its end, and the list opens with it highlighted and scrolled into view.
rules.highlight: The Menu's one sliding indicator (D-032): it follows the pointer and the arrow keys, fill/tertiary-hover with border/tertiary-hover. It is not the chosen option: the chosen option is marked by the check and by aria-selected only.
rules.keyboard: Focus stays on the trigger (role='combobox', aria-activedescendant names the highlighted option). Enter, Space, ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the list; ArrowDown and ArrowUp move (wrapping, like Menu); Home and End jump; Enter or Space chooses and closes; Esc closes and keeps focus on the trigger; Tab closes and moves on. A letter jumps to the next option that starts with it (the typed text resets after 500 ms); with the list closed it chooses that option straight away, like a native select. Clicking outside closes it.
rules.aria: Trigger: role='combobox', aria-haspopup='listbox', aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant while open, aria-labelledby the label and the value, aria-invalid, aria-describedby the hint or the error. List: role='listbox'. Option: role='option', aria-selected, aria-disabled. A name prop adds a hidden input, so the value posts with a form.
rules.states: rest, hover, open, focus (keyboard), invalid, disabled. The docs force each with the state prop.
rules.motion: Chevron as above. The list enters and leaves as the Menu does. The indicator slides as in the Menu.

well.$about: The trigger's surface. Border is an inset ring.

sidenav.$about: Side nav: one component for every sidebar (the HeyOz app and the docs site). Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule. This spec is the authority (D-002, D-030).
sidenav.title: Side nav
sidenav.anatomy: A column: logo row (logomark + wordmark, close button), brand picker, slot (e.g. search), groups of menu items (title + items), then the community card and the profile. Collapsed: a 54 rail of icons, the logomark opens it.

rules.states: Menu item: default, hover, active. Brand picker: default, hover. Hover and active add an inset border and the inner shade, so nothing moves. Active uses border/primary-active (D-035).
rules.shade: The nav, active and hovered items, the brand picker and its logo carry the inner shade (0, −4, blur 10, #000 50%). The community card carries the inner highlight. Figma effects, not tokens (D-021).
rules.light: Lit by light/cursor like everything else (D-020).
rules.scroll: Only the link list scrolls on short screens, so the brand menu and the footer are never clipped. It never passes the scroll to the page (overscroll contain). Its scrollbar is an 8px gutter kept in the nav's padding (items never change width), with the thumb shown only while the pointer is over the nav (D-037). Tooltips are fixed to the window.
rules.icons: Lucide. Item icons in a size/icon/md frame (20, vector 15). The 'opens in a new tab' arrow is a hint one step smaller: item.ext-icon, size/icon/sm (16, vector 12).
rules.collapse: Collapsed (54 rail), every item is 36 x 36 with its icon anchored left, never centred, so icons glide on one line while the width animates. Labels stay in place at zero width and fade (never display: none), so opening mirrors closing. Item height is fixed (40 open, 36 collapsed) so it animates instead of snapping. The logo row is never swapped: collapsed, the open button lies over the logomark, the wordmark fades and clips like a label and the close button fades out of the flow, so the logomark glides one way (16 to 10 from the nav edge) with no jump. Toggling from the logo row keeps keyboard focus on the toggle (open and close hand focus to each other); Ctrl+B leaves focus where it is, unless it is on one of those toggles, which hands over the same way. Width, spacing and size move at duration/slow; labels fade at duration/fast (D-031).
rules.shortcut: Ctrl+B / Cmd+B opens and closes the page's main nav. Ignored while typing in a field.

logo.$about: Logomark 32 and the wordmark. Close: a 32 ghost Button (xs) with a 16 panel-left-close icon. Collapsed: a 32 open button lies over the logomark; on hover or focus the logomark fades to a 16 panel-left-open icon.

title.$about: Group title, e.g. CREATION: label/sm/medium (11px), a quiet section label a clear step below the 16px items.

item.$about: v0-menu-item. 40 tall: 8 + 24 + 8. ext-icon: the arrow on items that open in a new tab.

tooltip.$about: Close sidebar / item names when collapsed. Secondary tier.

slider.$about: Slider: every value is a token reference, a plain even number (a set value in px, not a token) or a rule (D-025). Draft: the owner may still change it.
slider.title: Slider
slider.anatomy: A label row (label left, value readout right), then one row: [number field] track + thumb(s) [number field], then optional tick marks and min / max labels. Single value: one thumb, the track is filled from the start to the thumb. Range: two thumbs, the track is filled between them. The track is drawn by the component; the thumbs are native range inputs laid over it, so the keyboard and screen readers work as they do for any slider.

rules.native: Each thumb is an <input type=range>: role slider, aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and the name come from the element. aria-valuetext carries the formatted value, with its unit. A range slider is two inputs named "<label> minimum" and "<label> maximum" in one role=group named by the label. The inputs are transparent and ignore the pointer; only their thumbs take it. A press anywhere else on the control row (the whole 44 height, along the full width) jumps the nearest thumb to that point and carries on as a drag.
rules.hit: The control row is size/target (44) tall, so a press anywhere on it counts. The visible track is 8 and the thumb 20, centred in it.
rules.track: A well: fill/primary with an inset stroke/1 border, border/secondary, so it reads on every surface. Hover (pointer on the control) border/secondary-hover; dragging border/secondary-active (D-035). The border is an inset shadow drawn above the fill, so it never moves anything.
rules.range: The filled part is fill/inverse-active, one step below the thumb, and takes the inner shade. Hover and dragging turn it fill/inverse.
rules.thumb: The primary look (D-038, D-020): fill/inverse at rest, fill/inverse-hover on hover, fill/inverse-active while dragging, with the inner shade. A halo of 4 in the thumb's own colour at 24% shows on hover and 40% while dragging. The thumb never changes size and the halo is a shadow, so nothing moves. Effects are not tokens (D-021).
rules.focus: Keyboard focus (focus-visible) draws a border/focus ring of stroke/2 around the focused thumb. Nothing clips it: the control row is not a clipping container. Leave 6 free beyond each end of the track (ring 2 + halo 4) when the slider sits in a clipping container (D-037).
rules.tip: A value tag floats 8 above the thumb while it is dragged or keyboard-focused: fill/elevated, border/tertiary, radius/md, label/md/medium. It fades in at duration/fast and rises 4px; reduced motion keeps the fade. It is lit (D-020). It is aria-hidden: the input already announces the value.
rules.ticks: Optional marks below the track, one per step (up to 20 steps; more steps show 10 even marks, or the count you give). 2 wide, 4 tall, border/tertiary; marks inside the filled part use content/tertiary. They sit on the same centre line as the thumb, so a thumb lands exactly on its mark.
rules.limits: Optional min and max labels under the track ends, label/md/regular, content/tertiary.
rules.field: Optional number field beside the track (a plain <input type=number>, spin buttons hidden): fill/primary, border/primary, hover border/primary-hover, focus border/focus, radius/lg, height size/control/xs (32), body/md/regular. It follows the slider live while the typed number is inside the range, and snaps to the step and clamps to the range on blur or Enter. Range sliders get two fields, one at each end of the track. With a field, the value readout in the label row is dropped (it would say the same thing twice).
rules.keyboard: Tab goes to each thumb in turn (minimum, then maximum). Arrows: one step. Shift + arrows: ten steps. Page Up / Page Down: 10% of the range (at least one step). Home / End: the lowest and highest allowed value (a minimum thumb stops at the maximum thumb, and the other way round). Every change fires onChange; onChangeEnd fires when a drag ends, after a key press and after a field is committed.
rules.stacking: When two thumbs sit on the same value the one last used is on top; at the start of the range the maximum thumb is on top and at the end the minimum thumb, so one can always be pulled away.
rules.motion: State changes (halo, fill, border) run at duration/fast, easing/standard (D-031). The thumb and the filled part follow the pointer with no easing: they are the pointer position. Reduced motion keeps the fades and drops the tag's rise.
rules.disabled: Track fill/primary with border/secondary-disabled, range content/primary-disabled, thumb fill/inverse-disabled, label and value content/primary-disabled. No halo, no tag, the cursor stays an arrow, and the inputs leave the Tab order.
rules.when: Use a slider for a value on a continuous or finely stepped scale where the rough position matters more than the exact number: volume, opacity, duration, strength. Add the number field when people need the exact value. Use a segmented control for 2 to 5 named choices, a number field alone for an exact value on a wide range, and a switch for on / off.
rules.grid: Set values are on the 4px grid with 2px half-steps (D-025). Thumb 20, track 8, halo 4, tick 2 by 4, tag 24, field 72 wide.

value.$about: The value readout at the right of the label row.

track.$about: The well. 8 tall, a set value.

range.$about: The filled part of the track.

thumb.$about: 20, a set value. The primary look: inverse fill, inner shade.

tick.$about: Marks under the track: 2 wide, 4 tall, 4 below the thumb.

tip.$about: The value tag above a dragged or focused thumb.

limit.$about: The min and max labels under the track.

field.$about: The number field beside the track, a text field at size/control/xs.

switch.$about: Switch: a track and a thumb. On or off, effective at once. Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025). Status draft: the owner may still change it.
switch.title: Switch
switch.anatomy: A row: [track with thumb] [label + description], or [label + description] [track] when the label is on the left. The track is a rounded well; the thumb slides inside it. The whole row is the click target.

rules.states: Off, on; each at rest, hover, pressed, focus and disabled. Off is a well: fill/primary track with border/secondary, and a content/secondary thumb. On is fill/inverse (white, like shadcn's primary, D-038) with a content/inverse-primary thumb. Orange stays for the one main action (D-003).
rules.hover: Hover is the -hover fill and border of the track's own family (D-035); the off thumb lights to content/primary. Pressed is one step stronger, the -active fill and border. Hover and press work on the whole row, label included. Nothing moves or changes size: the border is an inset box-shadow.
rules.shade: No inner shade, unlike Button: at 16–20px the shade greys the white out, so on stays a flat, solid fill that pops (D-041). The track is a lit surface (D-020).
rules.motion: The thumb slides from one end of the track to the other, duration/base, easing/standard (D-031). Track colour and thumb colour change at duration/fast. The first paint never animates. Reduced motion: no slide, the thumb and track fade to the new state.
rules.size: sm: track 28 x 16, thumb 12. md: track 36 x 20, thumb 16. md is the default. The thumb sits 2 from the track's edge on every side. The thumb's travel is the track width minus the thumb minus 4. Text is the same in both: label body/md/regular, description body/sm/regular.
rules.label: Right of the switch by default. On the left (labelPosition start), the row can span the full width (block) so the switch sits at the far edge, as in a settings list.
rules.colours: Label content/primary, description content/tertiary. Disabled: label content/primary-disabled, description content/tertiary-disabled, track -disabled fill and border, thumb content/primary-disabled; a disabled on track uses fill/secondary-disabled, like a disabled primary Button, because fill/inverse-disabled is the same grey as the thumb.
rules.focus: Keyboard focus (focus-visible only) draws a ring outside the track: border/focus, stroke/2. The row never clips it. A scroll or clip container around a switch keeps stroke/2 of room (D-037).
rules.hit: The visible track is smaller than size/target (44) in height, and in width too. An invisible layer around the track makes the hit area at least 44 x 44 without moving anything. The label and description are part of the click target too.
rules.keyboard: Tab reaches each switch. Space toggles it. Enter does not. A disabled switch leaves the Tab order.
rules.aria: A native input type=checkbox with role=switch, so it works in forms and is announced as on or off. The label names it (aria-labelledby), the description describes it (aria-describedby). With no visible label, pass aria-label.
rules.use: Use a switch for a setting that takes effect the moment it changes, like turning a feature on. Use a Checkbox when a choice waits for a Save or Submit button, or when several options can be picked. The label names what is on ('Auto-save'), so on and off both read right; never label a switch with an action.
rules.light: The track is lit by light/cursor (D-020). The thumb sits inside it, so it is covered; the label is plain text and is not.

track.$about: The rounded well. Width is a set value (the height is an icon frame).

thumb.$about: The slider inside the track: track height minus 2 x padding.

off.$about: A well: darker than the surface it sits on.

tabs.$about: Tabs: switch between views of content, one at a time. A row of tabs with one underline that slides (D-032), and the panel each tab controls. Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025).
tabs.title: Tabs
tabs.anatomy: A tab list: a row of tabs on a 1px baseline, with one 2px underline under the selected tab. Each tab is a label, with an optional icon before it and an optional count after it. Under the list, one panel shows the selected tab's content.

rules.use: Tabs switch views of content: the pages of a settings area, the lists of a project (Assets, Brand, Members). Each tab owns a panel. Segmented sets a value (speed, alignment, resolution): it has no panels, it changes how something looks or works. If the choice changes what the page shows, use Tabs. If it changes a setting, use Segmented. Use 2 to 7 tabs; more than that, or a long list, belongs in a Select or a Menu.
rules.look: No frame and no fill: labels on a baseline. The selected tab has a 2px underline in content/primary, not orange, so orange stays for the one main action (D-003). The baseline is border/primary, 1px, the full width of the list. The underline sits on the baseline and covers it.
rules.sizes: md: 40 tall (size/control/sm), body/md/medium (14), padding x 12. sm: 32 tall (size/control/xs), body/sm/medium (12), padding x 8. Labels are always medium weight; the weight never changes with selection, so nothing shifts.
rules.tab: Label colour: rest content/secondary, hover and selected content/primary, disabled content/primary-disabled. The icon follows the label, and turns content/brand on hover like Button's ghost. Icon frame size/icon/sm (16), gap 6 between icon, label and count.
rules.hover: An unselected tab on hover shows a 2px rule under it in border/primary-hover, and pressed in border/primary-active (D-035: one step stronger, in its own family). The rule fades in at duration/fast; nothing moves or changes size. The selected tab's underline stays as it is.
rules.count: An optional count after the label: label/md/medium (12) in content/secondary on fill/tertiary, 20 tall, pill radius, padding x 6. On the selected tab the count is content/primary on fill/elevated. Counts are numbers or short text (99+); they are part of the tab's accessible name.
rules.motion: The underline slides from the old tab to the new one: position and width together, duration/base, easing/standard, in a straight line, the same duration whatever the distance (D-032). Labels and counts change colour in place at duration/fast (D-031). The first paint never animates. Reduced motion: no slide, a cross-fade. Panels swap with a fade at duration/base, easing/enter and no movement.
rules.activation: Automatic (default): arrow keys move focus and select, and the panel changes at once. Use it when panels are already loaded. Manual: arrow keys move focus only; Enter or Space selects. Use it when showing a panel costs a request or a layout jump.
rules.keyboard: The tab list is role tablist (aria-orientation horizontal) with aria-label. Each tab is role tab with aria-selected and, when it has a panel, aria-controls pointing at it. One Tab stop in the list: the selected tab (tabindex 0); the others are tabindex -1. Left and Right move to the previous or next tab and wrap at the ends; Home and End go to the first and last. Disabled tabs are skipped. Tab then goes to the panel.
rules.disabled: A disabled tab stays in the row, dimmed, as a disabled button (so it is also out of the Tab order). It is skipped by the arrow keys and cannot be selected. Never remove a tab that does not apply; disable it.
rules.overflow: When the tabs are wider than their container, the list scrolls sideways (D-037 scrollbar) and tabs never wrap or shrink. The selected tab scrolls into view when it changes. The edges that have more tabs behind them fade over space/24. The list is a scroll container, so it keeps stroke/2 of room on every side (padding, pulled back with a matching negative margin) and a focus ring is never cut. The baseline and the underline live inside the scrolling track, so they scroll with the tabs.
rules.focus: A stroke/2 ring in border/focus around the focused tab, radius/md, drawn outside the tab. It shows for keyboard focus only.
rules.panel: The panel sits space/16 under the list. It is role tabpanel, tabindex 0, labelled by its tab. Panels that are not selected stay mounted and are hidden (hidden attribute), so their state is kept and aria-controls always resolves.
rules.light: Tabs are not a surface: no fill, so nothing is lit. The count pill is a small lit fill.
rules.width: Hug (default): each tab is as wide as its content and padding, the row is as wide as its tabs and the baseline runs the full width of the container. Stretch: the tabs share the full width equally (use it on a narrow panel or a phone).

list.$about: The row. The track inside it carries the baseline and the underline.

tab.$about: One tab. Colours per state. The hover rule is a 2px line under an unselected tab.

textfield.$about: Text field: one component for a single line and for several lines (textarea), plus the field frame around it (label, hint, error, count). Every value is a token reference, a plain even number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-025). Status draft: the owner may still change it.
textfield.title: Text field
textfield.anatomy: A column: label row (label + optional marker), the control, the message row (hint or error on the left, character count on the right). The control is one frame, a well: [icon] [prefix] value [suffix] [trailing icon] [action button]. Single line: fixed height. Textarea: the same frame, min height of its rows, grows with the text up to its max rows, then scrolls inside.

rules.height: size/control/{size}: xs 32 (everyday), sm 40, md 48. Fixed for a single line. A textarea has this as the height of one row's frame; its min height is rows × line height + 2 × padding y.
rules.radius: Squircle like Button: height × 0.375 rounded to 4. xs 12 (radius/lg), sm 16 (radius/xl), md 20 (radius/2xl). Padding x is the Button's for the size: xs space/12, sm space/16, md space/20.
rules.well: D-036: a field is a well, darker than its surface: fill/primary at rest, with border/primary and the inner shade (0, -4, blur 10, #000 50%, D-021). It is a lit surface (D-020).
rules.border: stroke/1, drawn as an inset box-shadow, so no state moves anything.
rules.states: Rest: fill/primary, border/primary. Hover: fill/primary-hover, border/primary-hover. Focus: the border steps up to border/primary-active, nothing else: subtle, no ring (D-040). Invalid: border/critical (hover border/critical-hover, focus border/critical-active). Disabled: fill/primary-disabled, border/primary-disabled, value, placeholder, icons and label content/primary-disabled; not focusable. Read-only: looks like rest and does not change on hover, still focusable, value selectable and submitted, no clear button.
rules.focus: Focus is the frame's border stepping up (no ring, no outline). Focus on the clear or show button gives that button its own ring, not the frame. Clicking anywhere on the frame (not on a button) puts the caret in the input. The textarea clips only inside the frame.
rules.value: body/md/regular for xs and sm, body/lg/regular for md, content/primary. Placeholder content/tertiary. A placeholder is an example, never the label: it disappears when you type.
rules.icons: Leading and trailing icons are Lucide at size/icon/sm (xs, sm) and size/icon/md (md), content/secondary, 8 from the text. They are decoration and are hidden from screen readers. The control carries the meaning.
rules.affix: Prefix and suffix are text (https://, $, .com, USD) in the value's type and content/tertiary, inside the frame, 8 from the value. Clicking them focuses the input. They are read out with the field (aria-describedby).
rules.action: Clear and show/hide password are Button: ghost, icon-only, one step smaller than the frame, so it sits inside with equal room on three sides: xs field 28 (2xs) with 2 around it, sm field 28 with 6, md field 32 (xs) with 8. The inner radius is the frame radius minus that room, so corners stay parallel. Clear shows only when there is a value (fades at duration/fast, keeps its slot so nothing shifts), clears, and gives focus back to the input. Password: starts hidden, eye / eye-off, aria-pressed, label Show password / Hide password; the value never leaves the field.
rules.label: label/md/medium, content/secondary, space/6 above the control. A label is always present: visible, or aria-label when the design truly has none. 'optional' follows the label in label/md/regular, content/tertiary. Required fields get no marker; mark the optional ones instead.
rules.message: Hint and error use body/sm/regular, space/6 below the control. Hint content/tertiary. An error replaces the hint in the same row, content/critical, with a 12 alert icon so colour is not the only signal, and sets aria-invalid; the control points at it with aria-describedby. The row is a polite live region, so a new error is read out. When a field has a hint, an error swaps into the same height and nothing moves.
rules.count: Character count 'n / max' on the right of the message row, body/sm/regular, content/tertiary, tabular numbers, tied to the control with aria-describedby. It shows only when there is a max length, and the browser stops typing at max. It turns content/critical at max.
rules.textarea: Rows (min) default 3, max rows default 8. It grows with the text, one line at a time, as you type: the height follows the text with no animation, since an animated height would lag behind the caret. At max rows it scrolls inside with the global scrollbar (D-037). Padding y puts the first line where a single line sits: xs 6, sm 10, md 12. With auto grow off, the user resizes vertically with the corner handle.
