rules.motion: Fill, border, ring and colours animate at duration/fast, easing/standard (D-031). The clear button fades at duration/fast. Reduced motion keeps the fades; there is no movement to drop.
rules.keyboard: Tab enters and leaves. Esc clears a field that has a clear button and a value; it does nothing else. Enter submits the form, as a native input does; in a textarea it adds a line. The clear and show buttons are in the Tab order after the input (not while hidden).
rules.aria: Native input and textarea, label via htmlFor. aria-invalid on an error. aria-describedby: hint or error, count, prefix, suffix. disabled and readOnly are the native attributes. The password toggle is a button with aria-pressed, not a checkbox.
rules.use: Use a text field for free text of any length: names, URLs, prompts, notes. Use a select for a fixed list, a number field or slider for numbers, a switch or checkbox for yes/no. Use a textarea when the answer can run past one line, never to look big.

frame.$about: The well. Colours per state; every state keeps the same inset stroke/1 border.

message.$about: Below the control: hint or error on the left, count on the right.

toast.$about: Toast: a short message that says something happened, in a corner, and goes away by itself. It asks for nothing. Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule. This spec is the authority (D-025).
toast.title: Toast
toast.anatomy: One toaster per app: a fixed region in the bottom-right corner (full width at the bottom on narrow screens) holding a stack of up to 3 toasts. A toast is a card: a status icon, a message with an optional description, an optional action Button and a close Button.

rules.use: Use a toast to confirm something that already happened (Saved, Link copied, Clip deleted) or to report a background result (Export ready, Upload failed). Do not use it for a question or a decision (use a dialog), for an error on a field (show it at the field), for anything the person must not miss while it is the only record of it (use a persistent banner or dialog), or for messages that arrive in bursts (group them into one).
rules.api: toast(message, options) from anywhere, no provider. toast.success, toast.warning, toast.critical, toast.info set the type. Options: description, action { label, onClick }, duration (ms, Infinity keeps it), icon (a Lucide name), id (a toast with the same id is updated in place, its timer restarts), dismissible (default true). toast.dismiss(id) closes one, toast.dismiss() closes all. It returns the id. Render <Toaster /> once, in the root layout; a second Toaster renders nothing.
rules.types: neutral, success, warning, critical, info. The status shows on the icon only: the surface, border and text are the same for every type. Reason: a stack of tinted cards turns a corner of the screen into a traffic light and fights the content behind it, and tinted fills need their own text and border sets; the icon colour plus its own shape (check, triangle, cross, i) carries the type without relying on colour alone. Neutral has no icon unless one is given.
rules.surface: surface/tertiary, border/tertiary, radius/xl, the inner shade and the drop shadow (drop-md). It floats above the page and above dialogs (surface/primary), so it is one step lighter than both. A lit surface (D-020), and a light root, because it opens over other lit surfaces.
rules.live: The toaster is a region (aria-label Notifications) with aria-live polite, aria-relevant additions and text. Each toast is role status, except critical, which is role alert (assertive, interrupts). A toast never takes focus when it appears. F8 moves focus into the toaster (newest toast first, then its controls in order); Esc on a focused toast closes it and returns focus to where it was; Tab leaves the toaster normally. The close Button has aria-label Dismiss notification.
rules.time: Auto-dismiss: 5000 ms. With an action: 10000 ms, because an Undo that stays for minutes undoes something other than what the person remembers, and the pause rules below give time to reach it. Critical: stays until dismissed. All can be set with duration. The timer pauses while the pointer is over the toaster, while focus is inside it, and while the tab is hidden, and it resumes with the time that was left. With the toaster paused no toast leaves, so the stack never moves under the pointer.
rules.stack: At most 3 visible. The newest sits at the bottom, next to the corner where the eye already is; older toasts move up by the height of the newest plus the gap. A fourth toast removes the oldest non-critical one (critical toasts go last). Toasts move to their new place at duration/base, easing/standard (D-031), never snap.
rules.motion: Enter: the card fades in and rises region.travel (space/12) at duration/base, easing/enter. Leave: a fade at duration/fast, easing/exit, then the stack closes up. Swipe (touch and pen): drag sideways to follow the finger, release past 80px to dismiss, otherwise it springs back at duration/base. Reduced motion keeps the fades, drops the rise.
rules.placement: Desktop: bottom-right, region.width wide, region.inset from the right and bottom edges. Below 640: full width with region.inset-narrow on the sides and bottom, above the device's bottom safe area. A toast does not avoid a bottom sheet; the toaster sits above it (z-index 1070).
rules.actions: The action is a secondary Button, size 2xs (28). It runs its onClick and then closes the toast (action.dismiss false keeps it). At most one action. There is no brand Button in a toast (D-026, one per view). The close Button is ghost, size 2xs, icon only.
rules.static: A specimen for the docs only: the card without the toaster, the timer, the keys or the swipe. It is inert, so it leaves the Tab order.
rules.states: Action and close use the Button states. The card has no hover look: hover only pauses the timers and shows nothing, so nothing moves or changes size under the pointer.

region.$about: The fixed corner that holds the stack.

card.$about: One toast. Padding is 12 and 16 on the left so the icon sits where the text of a dialog would.

icon.$about: Status icon. Colour is the only place a status shows.

message.$about: The message. Its first line sits in a row the height of the buttons (28), so the icon, the text and the buttons share one centre line.

tooltip.$about: Tooltip: a short label that names or explains one control. One look for the whole system: the side nav's rail tooltips and the docs site's info tips switch to this component. Every value is a token reference, a plain number (a set value in px, not a token), 'none' or a rule (D-002, D-025).
tooltip.title: Tooltip
tooltip.anatomy: One bubble: a label of one short sentence, then an optional keyboard shortcut (one key chip per key). No arrow, no title, no buttons. It floats above the page, fixed to the window, beside the element it describes, 8 away.

rules.use: Use it to name an icon-only control, to add a shortcut, or to add one short extra fact to a control that already has a visible label. Never put the only copy of important information in it, and never anything the user must act on: it is hidden on touch, and it is gone as soon as the pointer or focus leaves. Longer or interactive content is a Popover. A control that already shows its own name and needs nothing more gets no tooltip.
rules.surface: surface/secondary with border/secondary, radius/md and the inner shade (0, -4, blur 10, #000 50%): the values the side nav's tooltip already used, so there is one tooltip look (D-021, D-036). It floats above other lit surfaces, so it is a light root (<Light>, D-020). No drop shadow and no arrow: the border and the 8 gap tie it to its control.
rules.text: label/lg/medium (14/18), content/primary. One sentence, no full stop, sentence case ('Close sidebar'), under about 60 characters. The bubble is as wide as its text up to the max width (240; 320 for the wide kind, e.g. a token's details), then wraps; a word that does not fit breaks. New lines in the text are kept. It never scrolls and never truncates.
rules.shortcut: A shortcut shows after the text as one chip per key (kbd): label/md/medium, content/secondary, fill/tertiary with border/tertiary, radius/xs, 16 tall and at least 16 wide, 2 apart, 8 from the text. Write keys as the user presses them: 'Ctrl', 'K'. The tooltip only shows the shortcut; the control must also work with it.
rules.timing: Hover: opens after 500 ms. That is long enough that a pointer crossing a toolbar shows nothing, and short enough that a pause feels answered. Warm: once a tooltip has been open, the next one opens at once while the pointer moves from control to control, and for 300 ms after the last one closed. An open tooltip closes at the moment the next one opens, so there is never more than one. Keyboard focus: opens at once, no delay. Leaving: 100 ms of grace, so the pointer can cross the 8 gap onto the bubble (it can be hovered and its text selected, WCAG 1.4.13); then it fades out. These are set values in components/tooltip-timing.js (DELAY, WARM, GRACE).
rules.dismiss: It closes on pointer leave, on blur, on Esc (even while the pointer is still over the control; Esc closes the tooltip and nothing else, a second Esc reaches the page or the popover around it), when the control is pressed (the user has seen it; it returns only after the pointer leaves and comes back) and when the control is removed or disabled.
rules.touch: Never on a touch-only tap or long press: hover does not exist there, so a tooltip would be a trap. Touch pointer events are ignored. Focus opens it only for keyboard focus (:focus-visible), never for a click or tap focus. So anything a tooltip says must also be findable another way.
rules.placement: top (default), bottom, left, right, centred on the control, 8 away (space/8). If the preferred side has no room and the opposite side does, it flips; if neither fits it takes the side with more room. It is then clamped to stay 8 (space/8) inside the window on every side, so near an edge it slides along the edge. It follows the control while the page scrolls or resizes. It is position: fixed in a portal on the document, so no scroll container or overflow: hidden ever clips it. Layer z-index 1090 (set value), above popovers.
rules.motion: Enter: fade, a 4 slide towards its final place from the control's side, scale from 0.98: duration/base, easing/enter (motion-pop, D-031). Left and right placements fade and scale only (motion-pop moves vertically). Leave: fade, duration/fast, easing/exit; it stays mounted until it has faded (usePresence). Reduced motion keeps the fade and drops the movement.
rules.aria: role=tooltip on the bubble, with an id. While it is open, the control gets aria-describedby pointing at it (added to any the control already has). A tooltip is a description, never the name: an icon-only Button keeps its own label (aria-label); when the tooltip text repeats that label, pass describe={false} so screen readers do not hear it twice. The control must be focusable: a disabled control gets no events, so wrap it in a focusable span or use aria-disabled.
rules.api: <Tooltip content="Save" shortcut="Ctrl S" placement="top"><Button .../></Tooltip>. The child is one element that accepts a ref (Button, a link, a native element). Props: content, shortcut (a string split on spaces, or an array of keys), placement, wide, delay, disabled, describe. TooltipBubble draws the same bubble inline, for documentation specimens.
rules.migrate: The side nav (data-tip, ::before, useTips) and the docs info tips (InfoTips, data-info) become <Tooltip> wrappers; both then lose their own tooltip code.

bubble.$about: The tooltip. Same values as the side nav's tooltip (surface/secondary, border/secondary, radius/md, padding 8 / 4, offset 8, label/lg/medium). Max widths 240 and 320 are set values.

kbd.$about: One key of a shortcut, inside the bubble.
